source: independent local remeasurement of downloaded actual RGB arrays and PNGs
findings: Aligned100 passes the original gate without any threshold or scoring change. Measured gain is approximately 1.91x in raw and actual policy frames.
Native 1.2 mm bar periods increase from approximately 2.47 pixels to 4.41 pixels in both orientations, with candidate sinusoid-fit R-squared above 0.91.

Policy vertical 2.4 mm bar period increases from 1.825 to 3.460 pixels; horizontal 2.4 mm grows from 2.99695 to 5.501 pixels. The baseline horizontal classification is borderline against the 3.0 threshold.
The unchanged baseline repeat and IOR=1 lens produce approximately 1.00x and do not pass; the 35-degree tilted lens loses the marked target and does not pass.

Aligned75 has visible nonlinear distortion: four corner markers remain a near-perfect quadrilateral while central patch locations differ from the affine map. Its 3.24x corner gain must not be described as uniform central magnification.

Raw and 224 gates can already pass different newly resolved pitches. Requiring raw to gain any new pitch is unnecessary if all raw baseline patterns are already resolved; keep current evidence unchanged and revise future gating only alongside a validated local-warp/ROI method.

Single-pixel policy markers, thin 0.8 mm black reference strip, fixed central 60-percent search region, and local affine patch lookup limit the metric. Normalized sinusoidal modulation may exceed 1 and is not calibrated Michelson contrast.
This validates rendered optical feasibility at one pose, not a task score, physical lens calibration, manipulation success, or a guaranteed real-world decoding gain.
